schema.title: Response Health Check Api Health Get

get.description: Resolve a url-safe slug to its exercise (the web Library's detail-page lookup).

patch.description: Edit a **custom** exercise. Renaming regenerates the slug, keeping the old one as an alias.

delete.description: Soft-delete a custom exercise, refusing to orphan the sets that reference it.

post.description:
On-demand fallback (docs/06): generate + persist this exercise's illustration if missing.

Returns the exercise; ``illustration_status`` is ``ready`` (with ``illustration_url``) on
success, or ``generating`` if a batch run is already producing it. 503 if the image
provider/Blob is unavailable.

get.description: The in-progress session, or `null`. May finish sessions abandoned >12 h (see the service).

post.description: Create a session and its sets in one transaction — all or nothing.
Create a session and its prescription in one transaction — a workout not yet performed.

get.description: A session's prescription in performance order, each line with its completion state.

post.description: Append lines to an existing session's prescription, transactionally.

get.description: Planned vs completed for one session, what is left, and what is next.

delete.description: Soft-delete a session and (with `cascade`) its sets, recalculating every PR affected.

post.description: Close a session, store its duration, and report adherence. Idempotent.
Log many sets into one session transactionally, with a PR verdict for each.

delete.description:
Soft-delete a set and recompute its exercise's records.

Returns the removed row rather than 204 so the caller has the id to `restore` with, and can
see it really was this set. The record it may have held falls back to the next best.

patch.description: Correct one line of a prescription. Never touches what was logged against it.

delete.description:
Soft-delete one prescribed line.

Returns the removed row rather than 204, for the same reason `DELETE /api/sets/{id}` does: the
caller gets the id to `restore` with. A set already logged against the line stays exactly where
it is and simply becomes off-plan work.

post.description: Log what was actually done against a prescribed line; normal PR detection applies.

Record a PR by hand — the REST twin of the MCP ``log_pr`` tool.

For records a logged set cannot express: an estimated 1RM, a hold timed outside a session, or
a PR migrated from another app. Overwrites whatever is stored for this exercise + metric.

patch.description: Correct a hand-entered record in place, without the delete-and-reinsert dance.

delete.description: Withdraw a hand-entered record; the next best becomes current rather than leaving a gap.
Remove one chronology entry, then rebuild the record from what is left.

post.description: Rebuild personal records and their chronology from the live sets + hand-entered claims.

get.description: Read-only: report any exercise whose record tables disagree with themselves.

post.description: Undo a soft delete and rebuild whatever records depended on the row being gone.
Hard-delete rows soft-deleted longer ago than ``older_than_days``. Irreversible.

get.description: Start Google sign-in: plant state/nonce/PKCE in a signed tx cookie, redirect to Google.
Validate the Google callback, verify the ID token, upsert the user, set the session.

ActiveSessionOut.title: ActiveSessionOut
ActiveSessionOut.description:
The user's in-progress session, or ``null`` when they aren't training.

Wrapped rather than returned bare so "no active session" is an ordinary 200 with a
typed, nullable field — clients poll this on every screen and a 404 would be noise.

``set_count`` lives here and **not** on :class:`SessionOut`, which is validated straight
off raw ORM rows at every other call site and would raise on a required field with no
matching attribute. It is here because it is what the callers of this endpoint actually
need next: both the docked session bar and the home workout card say "N sets" and would
otherwise fetch the entire session detail — every set plus full exercise rows — to count.

AdherenceOut.title: AdherenceOut
AdherenceOut.description:
How much of the prescription was done.

``percent`` is ``null`` when nothing was prescribed — neither 0 nor 100 is true of a session
that had no plan, and both would read as a judgement about one.

ClientRegistrationRequest.title: ClientRegistrationRequest
ClientRegistrationRequest.description: Inbound DCR body. Unknown RFC 7591 metadata fields are ignored, not rejected.

CompletedPlannedSetOut.title: CompletedPlannedSetOut
CompletedPlannedSetOut.description: The line that was just satisfied, and the set that did it (with its PR verdict).

ConnectionOut.title: ConnectionOut
ConnectionOut.description: A connected chat client + the state of the user's grant to it.

ExerciseCreate.title: ExerciseCreate
ExerciseCreate.description: Create a custom exercise. ``slug`` is derived from ``name`` when omitted.

ExerciseDeleteOut.title: ExerciseDeleteOut
ExerciseDeleteOut.description: What a custom-exercise delete did — or, with ``dry_run``, would have done.

ExerciseDetailOut.title: ExerciseDetailOut
ExerciseDetailOut.description: Full detail: adds the how-to steps + provenance/timestamps.

ExerciseOut.title: ExerciseOut
ExerciseOut.description: Catalog summary (list rows + nested group headers).

ExerciseProgressOut.title: ExerciseProgressOut
ExerciseProgressOut.description: One movement's share of the prescription.

ExerciseSetGroup.title: ExerciseSetGroup
ExerciseSetGroup.description: One exercise and its sets within a session detail.

ExerciseUpdate.title: ExerciseUpdate
ExerciseUpdate.description:
Patch a **custom** exercise; only supplied fields change.

No ``slug``: it is derived from ``name``, so the two cannot drift. Renaming keeps the old slug
resolvable as an alias.

FinishedSessionOut.title: FinishedSessionOut
FinishedSessionOut.description:
A closed session, plus how much of its prescription it covered.

Widening the finished session rather than wrapping it: the one field the UI reads off this
response is ``duration_minutes``, and every other caller treats it as a session. ``adherence``
is additive, so nothing that worked before has to change to keep working.

MeUpdate.title: MeUpdate
MeUpdate.description: Patch the current user's display preferences (Settings → units, docs/07).

MetricResultOut.title: MetricResultOut
MetricResultOut.description: What a rebuild produced for one (exercise, metric).

PlannedItemOut.title: PlannedItemOut
PlannedItemOut.description: A prescribed line with its movement and its completion state resolved.

PlannedSessionCreate.title: PlannedSessionCreate
PlannedSessionCreate.description: Create a session and its prescription in one transaction.

PlannedSessionOut.title: PlannedSessionOut
PlannedSessionOut.description: A session's whole prescription, in the order it is meant to be performed.

PlannedSetComplete.title: PlannedSetComplete
PlannedSetComplete.description:
What was actually done against a prescribed line.

Nothing is defaulted from the targets: a range of 8–10 has no single right answer, and a plan
recording its own prescription as the result would make adherence a tautology.

PlannedSetCreate.title: PlannedSetCreate
PlannedSetCreate.description: One line of a prescription. Every target is optional; a line with none is 'do a set'.

PlannedSetUpdate.title: PlannedSetUpdate
PlannedSetUpdate.description:
Patch one prescribed line; only supplied fields change.

``exercise_id`` and ``session_id`` are not here on purpose: moving a line to another movement
or another day is not an edit of that line, it is a different line.

PlannedSetsCreate.title: PlannedSetsCreate
PlannedSetsCreate.description: Append lines to a session's prescription — all or nothing.

PrCreate.title: PrCreate
PrCreate.description: A hand-entered record. ``unit`` is not a field — it follows from ``pr_type``.

PrDeleteOut.title: PrDeleteOut
PrDeleteOut.description: What is standing after a record was withdrawn — ``null`` if nothing supports one.

PrHistoryItem.title: PrHistoryItem
PrHistoryItem.description:
One entry in a record's chronology, auto or manual.

This replaces the ``SetOut`` this endpoint used to return. A manual record has no set behind
it, so a set-shaped payload could not represent one — which is precisely why manual entries
were missing from PR history before.

items.title: Items
items.description: Oldest first; manual and auto entries interleaved chronologically.

PrInfo.title: PrInfo
PrInfo.description: The PR verdict for the set that was just logged/updated.

PrUpdate.title: PrUpdate
PrUpdate.description: Correct a hand-entered record in place. Only supplied fields change.

RevokeConnectionOut.title: RevokeConnectionOut
RevokeConnectionOut.description: How many of the user's tokens were revoked for the client.

SessionDeleteOut.title: SessionDeleteOut
SessionDeleteOut.description: What a delete did — or, with ``dry_run``, would have done.

SessionDetailOut.title: SessionDetailOut
SessionDetailOut.description: Session plus its sets grouped by exercise (ordered by set number).

SessionProgressOut.title: SessionProgressOut
SessionProgressOut.description: Planned vs done for one session, plus what to do next.

SessionUpdate.title: SessionUpdate
SessionUpdate.description:
Patch session metadata; only supplied fields change.

``clear_notes`` rather than a nullable ``notes``: in a partial update ``null`` already means
"leave alone", so emptying a field needs its own word.

SessionWithSetsCreate.title: SessionWithSetsCreate
SessionWithSetsCreate.description: Create a session and its sets in one transaction (all or nothing).

SetBulkCreate.title: SetBulkCreate
SetBulkCreate.description: Log many sets into one session as a single transaction (all or nothing).

SetCreate.title: SetCreate
SetCreate.description: Log a set within a session (the session id comes from the path).

SetUpdate.title: SetUpdate
SetUpdate.description: Patch a set's metrics; only supplied fields change (PR is recomputed).

SkillOverviewItem.title: SkillOverviewItem
SkillOverviewItem.description: A skill flattened with the user's progress (defaults when not started).
